newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage insurance bill vote slated for Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage insurance bill vote slated for Wednesday.

text.p: House of Representatives has scheduled to vote Wednesday on a measure to curtail unneccessary mortgage insurance policies, majority leader Dick Armey's office said.
The House originally planned to vote on the bill, HR 607 known as the Homeowners Insurance Protection Act, on April 8 but the vote was postponed at the behest of the Republican leadership.
House Democrats blasted the delay at a press conference last week and accused Republicans of caving in to special interests.
Republicans said Tuesday the vote had been delayed only to craft a strategy for getting the Senate to approve the legislation.

"Between the time it was passed out of committee and the vote, people started to think about how it would move in the Senate," Armey spokeswoman Michele Davis said. "A stand-alone bill could be filibustered in the Senate."
The bill will still be considered on its own, however, Davis said. "People have gotten fairly comfortable about going ahead," she said.
Passed by the House Banking Committee on a 36-to-one vote last month, the bill would allow homeowners to cancel mortgage insurance when they build up sufficient equity.
Currently, mortgage lenders require a borrower to obtain and pay for such insurance when the borrower is making a relatively small downpayment, such as five percent of the purchase price of a home.
Borrowers putting down 20 percent or more generally are not required to obtain insurance, which can cost $300 to $900 a year.

The bill would automatically cancel a mortgage insurance policy if the homeowner was current on mortgage payments and had built up 25 percent equity of the original value of the house. Homeowner's equity is the value of the home after subtracting the remaining amount of principal on the mortgage.

Senate Banking Committee chairman Alfonse D'Amato, Republican of New York, has expressed strong support for the measure, but a committee session to amend and vote on a bill was postponed and has not been rescheduled yet.
